note: Attacker-controlled bytes enter the ip6-send fuzzer as the raw input buffer.
The first byte selects message settings while the remaining bytes stay attacker-controlled payload.
The payload is copied into an OpenThread message object, preserving attacker-controlled length and contents.
Append stores the supplied bytes into chained message buffers, making them available to later protocol construction.
When the stack builds an MLE Child Update Request, it appends network data from the leader into the outgoing message.
The TLV length is filled from the leader network-data store, which can exceed the fixed TLV buffer if the stored data is too large.
Appending the oversized TLV causes Message::Write/Append to read past the end of the stack TLV buffer, triggering the ASAN stack-buffer-overflow READ sink.
